clue.text: Tramp, for example, coming back from special spot

parts.note: to tramp is to plod, walk heavily

indicators.note: coming back tells us the abbreviation for 'for example' is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. is the Latin abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A vagrant returning from some special place, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a noun (a vagrant) but works as a verb. 'Coming back' turns EG into GE, and 'from' just joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A blotch or smudge of colour or dirt is a spot, a synonym in the informal British sense.

clue.text: Saw pair getting six balls bowled

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a pair getting six balls bowled at them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense or a tool, but is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a traditional saying, so the noun matches a wise maxim.

clue.text: Middle Eastener who's a bit of an egomaniac?

indicators.note: a bit of points to a run of letters found inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Asking if a man from the Middle East is somewhat self-obsessed.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Gulf state with its capital at Muscat is a person from the Middle East.

clue.text: Try small drinks, they twitter

parts.note: to have a go is to try
sips are small drinks

explanation.surface: Instruction to sample small drinks, birds twittering around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twitter' suggests birds or the social network, but here it means to chatter idly.
explanation.definitionFit: People who chatter idly about others are the ones who prattle, so the plural noun fits the pronoun.

clue.text: In Texas Union, does fashion mean suits?

indicators.note: In places the abbreviation for Union inside the one for Texas

parts.note: TX is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Texas

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so the letters of 'does' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether Texan unions' clothing choices amount to formal suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' turns DOES into EDOS; 'mean' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner jackets with matching trousers are formal evening suits, so the plural fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Foolish international group: "We welcome terrorists"

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations, an international group

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the pronoun wraps the terrorists

parts.note: taken as written
IS is the abbreviation for Islamic State, a terrorist group

explanation.surface: A world body saying it welcomes terrorists would be foolish indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking good sense or judgment, a synonym for foolish.

clue.text: Monkey about with game of chance, knocking heads off ornament

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for monkey is reversed

parts.note: an ape is a monkey in the loose sense

indicators.note: knocking heads off removes the leading letters, here the first two

parts.note: roulette is the casino wheel game of chance

explanation.surface: Fooling about with a casino game and lopping off some ornamental figures' heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns APE into EPA. 'heads' is plural, so two leading letters, RO, go from ROULETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative shoulder piece on a military uniform is an ornament, an example of the category.

clue.text: Run estate wearing sunglasses in Florida

indicators.note: wearing puts the run and estate inside the sunglasses, as a face wears them

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of lenses, so sunglasses
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an estate is land

explanation.surface: Someone running an estate wearing shades in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Florida' looks like a place for the scene but is the definition: a city there.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme-park city in central Florida is a place located in that state.

clue.text: Great northern runner?

parts.note: the British athlete who founded the Great North Run, the Tyneside half marathon, and was himself a distance runner

explanation.surface: A great runner from the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great North Run is a famous half marathon in north-east England; Foster, a Gateshead-born Olympic runner, started it.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a champion distance runner from the north and founded the Great North Run race.

clue.text: Try dancing to salsa, feet moving for exercise

indicators.note: moving means the letters picked out are shifted into a new order
feet are the bottoms, so in a word read down they are its final letters

explanation.surface: Advice to attempt salsa dancing, keeping your feet on the move, as a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' takes the last letter of each of the four words, Y, G, O, A, and 'moving' reorders them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian discipline of postures and breathing is a form of physical exercise, an example of the category.

clue.text: Company has party on board? What odd characters!

indicators.note: being on a ship means being aboard it, inside it, so the ship's letters wrap the rest

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel one goes on board
a crew is a company of people, especially on a ship
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: A ship's company throws a party aboard, and what a bunch of eccentrics they are.
explanation.walkthrough: By convention being 'on' board a ship (SS, steamship) means being inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric or crazy people are informally called oddballs, and this word is an American synonym for such characters.

clue.text: After first half of Enigmatist puzzle, one sees stars

indicators.note: to puzzle is to confuse, so those five letters are jumbled
half of a ten-letter word is its first five letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone half done with an Enigmatist crossword is seeing stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Enigmatist is a fellow Guardian setter, fitting the puzzle's theme of setters; 'puzzle' is a verb here, the anagram signal. 'After' and 'sees' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins are a zodiac constellation, a group of stars, so the name works as a definition by example.

clue.text: Listen to rock, no good being unable to leave home

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so the letters of 'Listen' are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone told to listen to rock music, a hopeless case who never moves out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rock' rearranges LISTEN into NESTLI. The definition reads 'being' as a noun: a creature unable to leave its home.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird too small to fly from its nest is a creature that cannot yet leave home.

clue.text: BASIC compiled two directions as co-ordinate values

indicators.note: a program written in BASIC is compiled, turning it into other code, so these letters are rearranged along with the directions

parts.note: S for south twice gives two compass directions
taken as written

explanation.surface: A program in the BASIC language, compiled, treats two directions as co-ordinates.
explanation.walkthrough: BASIC is an old programming language, and 'compiled' is the computing word that rearranges it with SS and AS.
explanation.definitionFit: On a graph, the horizontal x co-ordinate of a point is its distance along the axis, a mathematical term.

clue.text: Catholic church upset over books lacking bishop trials

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters over, so they are reversed

parts.note: URC is the United Reformed Church, a British denomination

indicators.note: lacking says the bishop's letter is taken from the books

parts.note: Bibles are books
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A Catholic church overturned over books with no bishop; quite a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses C plus URC into CRUC; 'over' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe test or ordeal is a figurative crucible, the melting pot where things are tried by fire.

clue.text: Illegally takes back furniture

indicators.note: back tells us the word for illegally takes is read in reverse

parts.note: someone who loots illegally takes goods

explanation.surface: Someone illegally repossessing furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat without a back or arms is a piece of furniture, an example of the category.

clue.text: Judge has opening for God

parts.note: the anus is the bodily opening at the end of the gut

explanation.surface: A judge gets an opening for God.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a chance for divinity, but 'opening' is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-faced Roman deity of doorways and beginnings gives his name to January.

clue.text: Address otherwise neat Spartan

indicators.note: an address is a speech, so the words are to be spoken out loud

parts.note: otherwise means or; neat, meaning cattle, is a steer, an ox

explanation.surface: A neat and spartan style of address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' plus 'steer' spoken in a non-rhotic British accent gives the answer. 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, so a steer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means severely simple and without comfort, the same as stern and plain.

clue.text: Rich, topless in El Salvador — such waste

indicators.note: in places the shortened word for rich inside the country code

parts.note: ES is the international code for El Salvador

indicators.note: topless says the word for rich loses its first letter

parts.note: affluent means rich

explanation.surface: A wealthy person going topless in El Salvador, and what a waste that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the A from AFFLUENT, leaving FFLUENT. 'such' links to the definition: waste of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid sewage or industrial discharge released into rivers is waste matter of that kind.

clue.text: Tips of nectarine and orange, all cooking in fat

indicators.note: cooking means mixing things up, so the letters are reordered
tips are the ends, here the first letter of each fruit

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe: fruit bits all cooking in fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips of' takes N and O; 'cooking' rearranges them with ALL, and IN is added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The greasy substance from sheep's wool is a natural fat used in ointments.

clue.text: Golden syrup runs clear, when poured into hollow tube

indicators.note: poured into puts the mixed letters inside the emptied tube
hollow says the inside of tube is emptied, leaving its outer letters
runs as of a liquid means to flow loosely, so the letters of clear are mixed

explanation.surface: Golden syrup flows clear when poured into a hollow tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like syrup flowing, but signals rearranging CLEAR into REACL.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden syrup is the British name for a pale form of this sugar-cane syrup, a synonym.

clue.text: Good time catching good bird

indicators.note: catching says the two pieces close round the second good

parts.note: pi is short for pious, good
an eon is a long period of time
pi is short for pious, good

explanation.surface: A pleasant time spent trying to catch a fine bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The common city dove is a bird, an example of the category.

clue.text: They manage sir's pain

indicators.note: to manage pain is to handle it, here the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A statement that certain things deal with a gentleman's pain.
explanation.walkthrough: This is close to an &lit: the pills are what manage pain. 'manage' rearranges SIRSPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Painkilling tablets are the things that manage pain, so the pronoun stands in for them.

clue.text: Boatman finally presses mute with debut of Ginger Spice

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word for a boatman
presses means squeezes out of shape, so the letters of mute are rearranged
a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A boatman silencing Ginger Spice of the Spice Girls with a press of the mute button.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice' looks like part of Ginger Spice, the Spice Girl Geri Halliwell, but is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The ground seed of a tropical tree is a kitchen spice used on custards and eggnog.

clue.text: Band's recordings

definitions.meaning: strips or bands of material, as the plural of band
audio or video recordings on magnetic strip

explanation.surface: A musical group's recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Band's' as a group's, but it stands for the plural of a strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic cassettes are recordings, and strips of material are bands; both senses share one word.

clue.text: Traditional London food the dessert contract delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: jelly is a dessert, a deal is a contract: jelly deal

explanation.surface: A traditional London dish is the one a pudding contract supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' looks like the contract being fulfilled, but it signals saying the words aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopped eels set in their own jelly are a classic cockney East End dish, sold at pie-and-mash shops.

clue.text: Mischievous fellow to choose one out for you

indicators.note: out for says the letter for one is swapped out in favour of the letter for you

parts.note: to pick is to choose
I is the Roman numeral for one
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A rascal is told to pick someone out for you.
explanation.definitionFit: The impish sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream is a mischievous fellow, a famous literary example.

clue.text: Dinner function government is winding up

parts.note: in northern Britain the evening meal, dinner, is called tea
sine, abbreviated sin, is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A government function at a dinner is closing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding up' looks like a closure but is the British slang sense of teasing someone; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang winding someone up means mocking or provoking them playfully.

clue.text: Heads will roll after Guardian loses middle ground

indicators.note: after says the rearranged heads come behind the newspaper's letters
losing its middle leaves just the first and last letters of the newspaper's name
rolling tumbles things around, so the letters of Heads are reordered

explanation.surface: Heads will roll at the Guardian after it loses its central ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like territory but is the past tense of grind, as teeth are ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinding one's teeth in anger is exactly what this verb describes, so the past tenses match.
